lead: Pakistan's Gulf commitments moved to centre stage: the Makkah pact's top committee, grouping Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, meets in Riyadh next week over Houthi attacks on the kingdom, the corps commanders endorsed the pact, and Ishaq Dar said more than six countries want to join. On security, two Pakistani civilians were killed by Indian border fire near Kasur and a CRSS tally showed violence-linked deaths up 83% in the third quarter. On money, the September trade deficit widened as Middle East shipping disruption threatened export orders, while the IMF and World Bank pressed for faster reforms.

stories.headline: Dar says more than six countries want to join Makkah pact
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar told a press conference in Islamabad that at least six Muslim countries had shown strong interest in joining the defence pact Pakistan shares with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. He did not name them in the reports.

stories.headline: Iranian airlines rejig Pakistan flights as US sanctions bite
stories.summary: Iranian carriers are rescheduling services to Pakistan after a run of cancellations, Arab News reported, as Washington's sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines squeeze the sector. Dawn read the Foreign Office's pledge to follow 'all applicable sanctions regimes' as a cautious shift from Islamabad's earlier stance.

stories.headline: Kandahar rejects army claim its governor hosted militant meeting
stories.summary: The military spokesman alleged that Kandahar's Taliban governor hosted a 26 August meeting of militant leaders discussing attacks inside Pakistan. Kandahar's administration called the claim baseless propaganda, BBC Urdu reported.

stories.headline: Two civilians killed by Indian border fire near Kasur
stories.summary: Pakistani security sources said India's Border Security Force shot dead two unarmed villagers from Ladhar and wounded a third after they went slightly beyond a border pillar, state radio reported via Dawn. Arab News said the two sides gave conflicting accounts of what happened.

stories.headline: Violence-linked deaths up 83% in third quarter, CRSS finds
stories.summary: The Centre for Research and Security Studies counted 1,415 deaths and 558 injuries in 385 incidents in July–September 2026, with Balochistan accounting for nearly 59% of fatalities. It named the TTP as the deadliest group, Dawn reported.

stories.headline: Seven militants killed in North Waziristan; policeman killed in Tank
stories.summary: Security forces killed seven militants in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan's Eidak area, state media said, citing security sources. Separately, attackers with guns and a grenade killed a policeman guarding a hospital in Jandola, Tank district.

stories.headline: Freed tanker crew due home as families of dead get compensation
stories.summary: Four of the ten Pakistani crew of the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 were due in Karachi on Saturday, Ishaq Dar said. The prime minister's office announced Rs12.5m and a house for each family of the three sailors killed during the vessel's recovery off Somalia.

stories.headline: Makkah pact committee to meet in Riyadh over Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Dar said the Strategic Political Defence Committee set up under the pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye will meet in Riyadh next week to review the surge in Houthi attacks on the kingdom.

stories.headline: Corps commanders back Saudi pact and warn against 'May 9-like' unrest
stories.summary: The 277th Corps Commanders' Conference, chaired by Field Marshal Asim Munir, endorsed the trilateral pact, condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and restated Pakistan's commitment to the security of the holy mosques. ISPR said any attempt to stir a 'May 9-like situation' at home would be met with decisive force.

stories.headline: Trade deficit widens 6% to $3.56bn in September
stories.summary: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data showed the monthly gap rising just over 6% year on year. Samaa reported the deficit for the first quarter of the fiscal year up 15.13% at $10.79bn.

stories.headline: Exporters warn Gulf shipping disruption puts orders at risk
stories.summary: Textile industry representatives said foreign buyers may defer or move orders as the US–Iran war raises freight costs and makes deliveries less predictable.

stories.headline: IMF commends oil-shock response but presses on gas reform
stories.summary: The Fund praised Pakistan's handling of the oil crisis and its power-sector recoveries, but sought faster progress on targeted gas subsidies and Rs3.6tr of circular debt. The two sides will discuss direct cash support for poorer power consumers next week, Dawn reported.

stories.headline: World Bank urges faster action under $20bn reform partnership
stories.summary: The Bank asked the government to speed up agreed measures, including sales-tax harmonisation and provincial farm-income and property taxes. It also proposed export-finance products for the EXIM Bank of Pakistan.

stories.headline: Petrol up Rs2.10 a litre as fuel subsidy reaches 7.5m people
stories.summary: Petrol rose to Rs392.76 and diesel to Rs399.64 a litre for 3–5 October. The government said more than 7.5 million people had drawn its targeted fuel subsidy since 15 September.

stories.headline: Centre may claw back Rs110bn power dues from provinces' NFC shares
stories.summary: The federal government is considering recovering about Rs110bn in power-sector dues by deducting them from provinces' National Finance Commission transfers, The Express Tribune reported.

stories.headline: KSE-100 slips 481 points on thin trading
stories.summary: The benchmark index closed at 168,155 as Middle East caution kept investors on the sidelines, extending the previous day's losses.

stories.headline: Government–PTI talks resume Saturday ahead of 4 October march
stories.summary: The first round chaired by Speaker Ayaz Sadiq ended without a breakthrough, while container blockades around Islamabad have left cargo piling up at Karachi port.

stories.headline: IHC to hear Imran Khan's £190m appeal on 5 October
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court set Monday to hear the former prime minister's appeal in the £190m case.

stories.headline: ECP proposes Punjab local elections on 14 December
stories.summary: The Election Commission sent a draft schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation.

stories.headline: Officials given a week to declare any dual nationality
stories.summary: The government warned officers they face action if they do not submit declarations on foreign nationality within a week, Geo News reported.
